review: Attack, grapple, collision, projectile and defense text inventoried with rapid-fire rows. Detailed techniques, special combat, injury, boundary reconciliation and executable validation remain pending.

entries.acceptance: Validate selected target, mode, readiness, reach and spatial access before attack roll. Resolve multiple attacks sequentially: each attack, eligible defense, then damage. Later attacks see consequences of earlier ones.
Attack uses effective skill; 3-4 critically hit and 17-18 miss. Reconcile low-score legality with general checks and critical rules without changing Lite dispatch.

One-handed weapons require the holding hand, two-handed weapons both hands; unwieldy weapons can become unready after use unless strength qualifies. Natural weapons require an unoccupied, unrestrained body part and suitable access.

Declared melee deception exchanges each -2 effective attack skill for -1 defense against this attack, keeping final attack skill at least ten. A campaign can instead restrict choice to -4/-2. Validate before rolling.
Ordinary or committed melee attack can replace exactly one available attack with two at -6 each, using ready weapons. Different targets are allowed; do not recursively split additional attacks.

Grabbing a held item needs an empty hand or a suitable grabbing weapon; attack dexterity or grappling skill at -4 with normal defense. On later turns, each full-turn regular strength contest transfers the item on victory or loses grip on defeat; retain unresolved ties under regular-contest rules.
Grappling requires a free hand and close range, uses dexterity or grappling skill and normal defense, and causes no initial damage. Evaluation and feint can apply. Record participants and held parts.

Torso grapple imposes -4 dexterity and prevents departure unless target strength exceeds twice holder strength, in which case holder becomes encumbrance. B371 instead allows movement at equality; preserve this boundary discrepancy for a documented policy.
Each committed arm after the first two adds +2 to the grapple attack. Occupied arms cannot parry. Release is free on the holder’s turn, with per-arm occupancy updated.

To grapple a prone, kneeling or seated target, holder kneels or lies unless target size exceeds holder by at least two. The posture adjustment can use the attack’s step; reconcile this specific permission with ordinary posture transitions.

Targeted grapples use half the normal location penalty; dexterity -4 applies only to that part. Specify rounding through B400. Holding an arm/hand permits a later regular strength contest to force release, but not automatically take the weapon.

After grappling a standing target, compare each participant’s best strength, dexterity or grappling skill; nonstanding initiator takes posture attack penalty. Loser falls and releases any grip on winner; tie changes nothing. Initiator selects legal adjacent footprint for a fallen target.

Pin requires a grounded target held by torso. Regular strength contest adds +3 per size difference to larger participant and +3 to the participant with more free hands. Victory pins; defeat/tie does nothing. Holder stays to maintain pin but can free one hand.

Neck hold uses strength against the higher of victim strength/health. One hand gives -5, each beyond two +2. A larger holder can squeeze torso at -5 unless possessing the body-constriction capability. Victory deals crushing equal to victory margin through normal armor; neck injury uses 1.5 factor.

Any qualifying damage through protection, including blunt trauma, starts one fatigue loss on each victim turn until escape. Link suffocation to the actual hold and avoid a second environmental charge for the same cause.
Choke, joint lock and neck/limb twist depend on specified skills, held locations and B403-B404 procedures. A generic grapple state does not implement these techniques.

A holder can bite or use close-reach natural strikers with hands occupied; free hands permit close attacks or ready actions. Aim, feint, concentration, wait and ranged attacks require the victim to be pinned.

Pinned targets can be moved within lifting/dragging and encumbrance limits. Without a pin, departure releases the target unless holder strength is at least twice target strength; sufficiently strong holders may carry/pull instead.

Held actors cannot use captured limbs or bite with held head/neck; allowed attacks are unarmed or close-reach weapons. Aim, feint, concentration, wait and ranged attacks are prohibited. A pin prohibits physically moving maneuvers.
A free hand permits readying with dexterity check; failure drops the item. Ability toggles requiring ready succeed without this extra check.

Escape is a quick strength contest. Holder receives +5 for two hands, or pin bonuses +10 with two/+5 with one. Additional arms beyond two add +2 to the relevant participant; stunned holder takes -4. Unconscious holder releases automatically. A successful escape permits immediate one-yard movement.
Pinned escape attempts occur at most once per ten seconds. Store the deadline on the restraint episode so recreating a request cannot reset it.

Collision attack uses dexterity or eligible brawling/sumo skill and bypasses move-and-attack melee -4/cap-nine. Mount attacks use riding; vehicle attacks operation skill, with mount/vehicle health capacity for damage.

After target dodge, move at least two yards beyond if allowance remains; resolve other targets or obstacles in the path. A solid-obstacle collision applies attacker’s damage to self and optionally obstacle.

Each participant inflicts crushing dice equal to own health capacity times relative speed divided by 100. Head-on speed includes opponent’s prior-turn approach. Fractions up to .25/.5/below one use 1d-3/1d-2/1d-1; at least one die rounds half upward. Strong committed option can increase damage.

Compare damage rolls: equal or greater attacker damage forces target dexterity to avoid falling; at least double knocks target down automatically. Opponent damage at least double instead knocks attacker down. Resolve zero-value ties and interaction with armor using detailed collision rules.

Flying tackle requires at least two legs and one free arm, gives +4 attack and one additional reach, and permits jumping skill. Attacker ends lying whether attack succeeds or fails, with legal shared footprint.
Four-or-more-legged pounce uses tackle with a dexterity, acrobatics or jumping check to remain standing. A mounted rider checks riding-4 to avoid falling.
Shield collision uses shield skill, adds shield defense bonus to damage and assigns incoming collision damage to shield. Attacker can still fall when opponent damage doubles own basic damage.
One/two-handed shove uses dexterity or sumo skill with normal defense; double thrust crushing, applying -1 per die for one hand. Result causes knockback only, never direct injury.

Projectile spells and eligible attack abilities use ranged attack rules; aura, direct resisted and melee modifiers can change classification. Do not route every supernatural effect through weapon attack.
Require distance within maximum and any minimum range. Half-damage distance affects damage rather than legality. Use actual weapon or ability definition.

Combine range yards and applicable speed yards/second before lookup, choosing the larger penalty between boundaries. Optional human-speed simplification ignores speed through movement ten except flight, sprinting and similar cases; record policy.
Thrown items leave inventory and ready state whether they hit or miss. Use strength-based range or specific catalogue definition; later reuse requires retrieval and readying.
Thrown attacks permit block/parry. An unarmed parry succeeding by at least five or critically catches the weapon; update hand occupancy and inventory atomically.
Muscle-powered projectiles use wielder strength except bows/crossbows use weapon strength where specified. Do not substitute current character strength for a fixed weapon rating.

Shots and reload duration determine owned ready progress. Magazine/belt replacement restores capacity with actual ammunition; individually loaded weapons gain one shot per interval unless a qualifying loader changes it.
Declare positive shot count before rolling, bounded by firing rate and loaded ammunition. One burst uses one attack roll and one ammunition expenditure, not one attack per projectile.
On successful rapid fire, hits equal one plus floor(success margin/recoil), limited to shots fired. Spraying, suppression and special projectile types require separate B408-B409 procedures.

Defense requires awareness of attack possibility and freedom to react; forbidden maneuver, unconsciousness, immobilization or unawareness denies defense before any roll. Critical hits deny active defense.
Defense rolls 3-4 succeed even with effective defense one or two, and 17-18 fail. Never reuse a general low-target rejection that suppresses these permitted defense rolls.
Stun gives -4 defense. Shock never penalizes active defense; temporary attribute effects require their separate rules.

Ready shield bonus applies to dodge, parry and block from front or shield side for melee, thrown and muscle-powered projectiles. Firearm eligibility requires the optional shield-damage procedure; do not globally add shield bonus.
Dodge is floor(basic speed+3) minus encumbrance level. Permit repeated dodges against different attacks without a cumulative count penalty; one dodge per given attack.
Successful dodge removes one hit plus success margin; critical dodge removes all hits in that attack. Retain remaining hits for independent damage resolution.
Requires invested acrobatics, or aerial skill while flying; once per actor turn. Roll before dodge: success adds two, failure subtracts two. May combine with retreat; store usage even on failure.

Declare protective dodge after attack succeeds but before ally defense, with legal step to intercept. Success transfers hit to protector; failure preserves ally defense. Either attempt prevents protector retreat until next turn, and cannot combine with retreat.
Vehicle dodge uses floor(operator skill/2)+handling with actual evasive maneuver eligibility, not personal speed+3.

Block requires ready shield/cloak or legally lifted body, score floor(skill/2)+3. Permit melee, thrown, projected liquids and muscle-powered missiles, not bullets/beams. One block attempt per turn, even on failure.
Parry requires ready weapon or eligible empty hands. An unbalanced weapon used to attack this turn cannot parry. Apply actual weapon defensive modifier.
Parry is floor(skill/2)+3 plus applicable modifiers. Off-hand -4 skill gives -2 parry unless exempted; do not subtract both.

Ordinary parry covers melee and thrown attacks. A nearby ranged attacker within reach may have the weapon/arm parried rather than the projectile. Special distant projectile defenses require their capabilities.
Track attempts per weapon/hand per actor turn: repeated penalty is -4, reduced to -2 for fencing or eligible mastery, and -1 for both. Reset at the actor turn boundary, not on a new attacker.
Thrown-weapon parry penalty is -1 normally or -2 for objects of at most one pound.

After armed parry of an unarmed attack, optional immediate weapon skill check can injure the attacking limb with no defense. Check takes -4 for specified trained striking/grappling attack skills. Damage uses the parrying weapon.
Author assigns a suitable skill to improvised defensive objects. A bow loses bow function after one parry even if usable briefly as a club. Most improvised objects use cheap breakage quality.

Handless creatures cannot use ordinary unarmed parry. Eligible boxing/brawling/throwing/striking skills or higher dexterity use one hand; wrestling/sumo require two. Weapon parry penalty is -3 except thrusts or designated trained skills. Respect individual skill restrictions.
With hit locations enabled, failed unarmed parry against a weapon lets attacker choose original location or parrying arm. Apply location injury once, including actual crippling threshold.

Natural strikes count as weight strength/10; body collisions count as full strength. Weapon parrying at least triple its weight risks breakage: 2-in-6 at triple, +1 per further whole multiple, quality +2 cheap/-1 fine/-2 very fine.
A broken parrying weapon still defends unless breakage odds exceeded six-in-six. Preserve pre-roll odds and distinguish automatic breakage from invalidated defense.

A one-handed/unarmed parry cannot stop weight exceeding basic lift; two-handed limit is twice basic lift. Attack proceeds; surviving weapon drops, or unarmed defender moves back one yard and checks dexterity against falling. Resolve breakage and relocation atomically.

Retreat is a legal away-step added to melee defense: dodge +3, block/parry +1, selected mobile unarmed/fencing parries +3. It does not cancel reach for the triggering attacker’s remaining attacks; bonus persists against that attacker until next turn.
An attacker with unused permitted step may follow retreat. Preserve step expenditure and the order of reactions.
One retreat per actor turn; reject while sitting, kneeling, stunned, or after movement faster than basic move on previous turn. Lying actors can roll away. Require a valid destination.
Ranged dodge-and-drop gives +3 and leaves actor prone; bonus applies against that foe for the turn. Newly reached cover protects subsequent attacks but not the triggering attack.

Protective dodge-and-drop within a step puts both actors prone on success; protector takes hit unless success margin is at least three, when neither is hit. Intercepting an explosive creates a contact explosion under B415.

Against area/cone/explosion, a legal step can reach cover or increase blast distance. Success moves before effect; failure applies effect before movement. Flying/swimming dodge-and-drop requires concealment below and does not create prone posture; blast-distance diving remains possible.
Firing 2 through 4 shots gives attack bonus +0. Validate both boundaries and use committed shot count.
Firing 5 through 8 shots gives attack bonus +1. Validate both boundaries and use committed shot count.
Firing 9 through 12 shots gives attack bonus +2. Validate both boundaries and use committed shot count.
Firing 13 through 16 shots gives attack bonus +3. Validate both boundaries and use committed shot count.
Firing 17 through 24 shots gives attack bonus +4. Validate both boundaries and use committed shot count.
Firing 25 through 49 shots gives attack bonus +5. Validate both boundaries and use committed shot count.
Firing 50 through 99 shots gives attack bonus +6. Validate both boundaries and use committed shot count.
Beyond the 50–99 band, each doubling increases the rapid-fire attack bonus by one. Verify integer band boundaries independently.
